text:
alex: hi all — first week here, trying to start the local stack. docker-compose spins up the db container but my app gets: "could not connect to server: No such file or directory" when connecting via unix socket. I tried "psql -h /var/run/postgresql -U postgres" and also using the socket path in the DSN. Any quick tips? is socket vs tcp a thing on mac w/ docker?

morgan: welcome! :wave: short answer: with Docker it's usually easier to use TCP (localhost + port) instead of unix sockets. containers expose a TCP port, sockets are host-local files and don't always map cleanly across the Docker boundary on macOS.

ajamie: fwiw, on mac/docker-desktop the container's socket file isn't visible to the host unless you mount it specifically and deal with permissions. so yep, use a port mapping in compose and connect to localhost (or host.docker.internal) from the host app.

lee: example docker-compose snippet we use for local dev — make sure db binds to 0.0.0.0 inside the container so port mapping works:

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - ./tmp/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

Then from your host: `psql postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres`

morgan: also check if you have a local brew/postgres running — that can conflict with the port. `lsof -i :5432` or `pg_ctl status` depending on how you installed it.

alex: ah, i did have brew postgres running. stopped it and the tcp connect works now. thanks — curious: is there any reason to use unix sockets at all for local dev?

jamie: sockets are marginally faster and avoid TCP overhead, but for dev it's more friction. some apps detect unix sockets by default (rails) which can surprise you. For CI or on-host installs sockets make sense; dockerized workflows typically use TCP.

lee: If you really want to use a socket, you'd need to mount the host directory into the container and set `unix_socket_directories` in postgres.conf, and ensure ownership matches `postgres` user. Example quick fix: `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./tmp/postgres` (where 999 is postgres uid in that image) — but fragile.

alex: good to know. i also saw errors about "permission denied" when mounting volumes earlier — that explains it.

morgan: one more troubleshooting tip — check container logs: `docker-compose logs -f db` and inside the container: `docker-compose exec db psql -U postgres -c "select 1"` to confirm DB is healthy.

devbot: Reminder: infra runbook for dev envs is at https://intra.redwood/dev-runbooks/local-db (internal) — includes tips for mac m1, volume perms, and common ports.

alex: awesome, fixed it by stopping brew postgres and re-creating the compose volume. thanks everyone :tada:
